entries.text: Open the kelpie repo and show me the current architecture in a diagram.

The user wants an architecture overview of the kelpie desktop prototype. I know the layout: a Tauri shell, an in-process Rust control plane, and a React frontend. I will draw the three-layer structure and label the data flows.

Here is the kelpie desktop architecture as it stands: ```mermaid flowchart LR R[React frontend
TypeScript + Vite] -- "commands + events" --> T[Tauri 2 shell
Rust] T -- "in-process core" --> C[Control plane
herdr client + omp projections] C -- "NDJSON RPC over unix socket" --> H[herdr 0.7.5] C -- "session JSONL (incremental)" --> O[omp session files] H -- PTY --> A[agent panes] O --> A ``` **Key properties:** | Layer | Language | Talks to | | --- | --- | --- | | Frontend | TypeScript / React | Tauri commands + events | | Shell | Rust (tauri) | in-process core | | Core | Rust | herdr socket + session files | - No HTTP loopback for the desktop app; the bridge stays as the mobile mode. - Transcript parsing is offset-based, so 200 MB sessions stay cheap. - Usage comes from `omp usage --json --redact`.

entries.text:
The layout is small and layered:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as You
    participant F as React UI
    participant B as Tauri core
    participant H as herdr
    U->>F: open agent chat
    F->>B: session(paneId)
    B->>H: session.snapshot
    H-->>B: fleet state
    B-->>F: fleet + poke events
    F-->>U: rendered transcript
```
